args.title: redline-review-memorandum.docx
args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Concession Agreement — TxDOT Counterparty Markup
Energy & Natural Resources
Matter File 13 — Confidential / Attorney-Client Privileged

TO:      Deal Team / Client Counsel
FROM:    Energy & Natural Resources Practice
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
RE:      Comparison of TxDOT Markup Against Original Draft, Negotiation Playbook, Lender and Surety Letters, and Financial Model — Risk Ratings and Counter-Proposal Language
OUTPUT:  redline-review-memorandum.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum reconciles the Texas Department of Transportation ("TxDOT" or "Counterparty") markup of the draft Concession Agreement against (i) our original firm draft, (ii) the firm negotiation playbook for energy/natural-resources concession transactions, (iii) lender and surety side letters, (iv) the project financial model, (v) Disclosure Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B (survival matrix), and (vi) the controlling deal-team instruction in the latest partner correspondence.

The Counterparty revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four material deviations that must be addressed before execution:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap;
  (2) Conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible (true deductible) to a tipping (threshold) basket;
  (3) Expansion of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs to exclude regulatory action of the type already disclosed and at issue on this project; and
  (4) Shortening of the survival / limitation period for core representations, in direct conflict with Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email — supersedes earlier thread messages): the client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket), but treats ANY reduction of the survival period for core representations as a WALK-AWAY issue. All recommendations below implement that priority ordering.

Risk-rating scale used throughout:
  • HIGH     — Walk-away or near-walk-away; financing / surety / model breakage risk, or client red-line.
  • MEDIUM   — Material economic or risk-allocation shift; counter required; negotiable with trade.
  • LOW      — Acceptable with clarifying language or ministerial clean-up; limited residual exposure.
  • CONCEDE  — Client-authorized concession per controlling deal-team instruction.

================================================================================
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED AND SCOPE
================================================================================

A. Operative Base Materials
   • Original firm draft Concession Agreement (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, termination).
   • Firm negotiation playbook — energy & natural resources concession precedent (indemnity architecture, MAE formulation, survival matrix, regulatory risk allocation).
   • Lender side letter(s) conditioning availability / draw and MAC/MAE definitions on indemnity and survival terms consistent with the base draft.
   • Surety letter(s) / bond underwriting conditions tying penal sum, indemnity back-to-back, and claim windows to the base survival and cap structure.
   • Project financial model (contingency, retained-liability, and indemnity-recovery assumptions embedded in coverage ratios and reserve sizing).

B. Counterparty Markup
   • TxDOT revision accepting most firm-standard provisions subject to the four deviations identified in Section III.

C. Schedules and Exhibits (control over general base statements)
   • Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup's MAE regulatory carve-outs.
   • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift.
   • Exhibit B — survival matrix contradicted by the markup's limitation-period change.

D. Deal-Team Correspondence (controlling instruction)
   • Latest partner message: concede basket conversion; survival-period reduction is walk-away.
   • Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are SUPERSEDED and are not relied upon.

E. Excluded
   • Misfiled administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement (administrative file / distractor). Contents were not used.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Base draft / playbook: Firm-standard aggregate indemnification cap sized to [playbook percentage of concession value / model-backed recovery assumption], with customary carve-outs from the cap for fraud, willful misconduct, and fundamental representations.

TxDOT markup: Cap is reduced without blackline call-out or conforming edits to related definitions, schedules, or the damages limitation clause ("silent" reduction).

Schedule / exhibit interaction:
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. A lower cap would silently shift residual exposure for those retained items back onto the Concessionaire / project company once the reduced cap is exhausted, contrary to the risk allocation assumed in the base draft and the financial model’s indemnity-recovery line items.
  • Lender letters typically require that the borrower/concessionaire indemnity package remain capable of covering scheduled retained liabilities up to the modeled amount; a silent haircut creates a financing conditionality gap.
  • Surety underwriting often back-to-backs indemnity recovery to the contractual cap; a reduced cap can force re-pricing or reduced penal-sum support.

Financial model impact: Lowers expected recoverable indemnity, increasing net contingency draw and stressing DSCR / lock-up metrics if a Schedule 5.2 liability crystallizes above the new cap.

Risk rating: HIGH (MEDIUM if limited to a modest, disclosed haircut with Schedule 5.2 true-up; as drafted — silent and unquantified — treat as HIGH).

Recommendation: REJECT silent reduction. Require full restoration of the base-draft cap, or, if a commercial compromise is authorized, an express, quantified cap with (i) Schedule 5.2 liabilities carved out of the cap or subject to a separate special indemnity uncapped / higher-capped stack, (ii) conforming edits to the damages limitation and definitions, and (iii) lender and surety bring-down consents.

Counter-proposal language:

  "Section [X.X] (Limitation on Indemnification). The aggregate liability of [Indemnifying Party] under this Article [X] shall not exceed the Cap Amount; provided, that the Cap Amount shall not apply to (a) Fraud or Willful Misconduct, (b) breaches of Fundamental Representations, or (c) any Retained Liability set forth on Schedule 5.2. 'Cap Amount' means an amount equal to [__% of the Concession Value / $____], being the amount set forth in the firm draft dated [date] and not any reduced figure appearing in any markup that has not been expressly initialed by both Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, no silent or conforming-edit-only reduction of the Cap Amount shall be effective."

  Special-indemnity rider (if commercial haircut on general cap is later authorized):

  "Notwithstanding Section [X.X], [Indemnifying Party] shall indemnify the Indemnified Parties from and against any Loss arising out of or relating to the matters set forth on Schedule 5.2, without application of the Cap Amount, up to a separate Schedule 5.2 Cap of $____ (or, if blank, without aggregate limitation other than actual Loss)."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Base draft / playbook: True deductible basket — Indemnifying Party liable only for amounts in excess of the basket; amounts below the basket are absorbed by the Indemnified Party and do not "tip" first-dollar recovery.

TxDOT markup: Converts the basket to a tipping (threshold) basket — once claims in the aggregate exceed the basket, recovery is from dollar one.

Schedule / exhibit interaction:
  • Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities become more fully recoverable once the tipping threshold is crossed, partially offsetting (but not curing) the cap reduction in Deviation 1.
  • Model assumes deductible treatment (first-loss retention). Tipping treatment is more favorable to the Indemnified Party / client side on recovery timing and quantum once the threshold is met.

Lender / surety: Generally neutral to slightly positive for lenders/sureties supporting the Indemnified Party; no playbook prohibition on tipping baskets when granted as a negotiated concession.

Controlling client instruction: CONCEDE the basket conversion.

Risk rating: CONCEDE (client-authorized). Residual drafting risk only — ensure the tipping mechanic is express, the basket quantum is unchanged unless separately agreed, and Schedule 5.2 / fundamental / fraud claims remain basket-exempt per playbook.

Recommendation: ACCEPT conversion to tipping basket; clean up drafting so the mechanic is unambiguous and carve-outs from the basket are preserved.

Counter-proposal language (implementing the concession cleanly):

  "Section [X.Y] (Basket). No indemnification shall be payable under Section [general indemnity] unless and until the aggregate amount of all Losses indemnifiable thereunder exceeds $[Basket] (the 'Basket'), in which event the Indemnifying Party shall be liable for all such Losses from the first dollar (and not merely the excess over the Basket). Claims arising from (i) Fraud or Willful Misconduct, (ii) breaches of Fundamental Representations, or (iii) Retained Liabilities on Schedule 5.2 shall not be subject to the Basket and shall be recoverable from the first dollar without regard to the Basket."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — MAE Definition: New Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Base draft / playbook: MAE definition includes material adverse changes arising from regulatory action, enforcement, or adverse determinations affecting the concession, the project, or the Concessionaire's ability to perform — subject only to narrow, market-standard carve-outs (general changes in law applicable to similarly situated parties, etc.), with customary disproportionate-impact "add-backs."

TxDOT markup: Adds carve-outs for "regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter," which — read against Schedule 3.7 — would exclude the two pending regulatory inquiries (and their outcomes) from MAE / closing-condition / termination analysis.

Schedule / exhibit interaction:
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect, and are the factual predicate for, the markup's new MAE regulatory carve-outs.
  • If the carve-outs stand, an adverse resolution of either Schedule 3.7 inquiry could neither support an MAE walk-right nor feed related termination / condition-failure remedies, leaving the client holding project risk the base draft allocated to the Counterparty / closing conditionality.
  • Playbook rule: scheduled disclosure qualifies representations; it does not, without express agreement, rewrite the MAE definition to neutralize the very risk disclosed.

Lender / surety / model:
  • Lender MAC/MAE bring-down and drawstop mechanics are typically cross-wired to the Concession Agreement MAE. Carving out the live regulatory matters creates daylight between project-level and financing-level MAE, risking involuntary default or unavailable draws if lenders retain a broader MAE.
  • Surety underwriting of performance / payment product is sensitive to open regulatory exposure; neutralizing MAE on known inquiries may trigger requalification.
  • Financial model contingency does not fully absorb a severe adverse regulatory outcome on both Schedule 3.7 items; MAE/termination optionality is part of the risk stack.

Risk rating: HIGH

Recommendation: REJECT the broad regulatory-action carve-out as applied to Schedule 3.7 matters. Limited compromise: permit a carve-out only for generally applicable changes in law or generally applicable regulatory programs, with a disproportionate-impact add-back, and expressly preserve MAE treatment for project-specific enforcement, adverse orders, permit denial/revocation, or material expansion of the Schedule 3.7 inquiries.

Counter-proposal language:

  "'Material Adverse Effect' means any event, change, circumstance, development, effect, condition, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, condition (financial or otherwise), or results of operations of the Project or the Concessionaire, (b) the ability of [Party] to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby or to perform its obligations under the Concession Documents, or (c) the validity or enforceability of any material Concession Document; provided, that 'Material Adverse Effect' shall exclude any event, change, circumstance, development, effect, condition, or occurrence to the extent arising out of generally applicable changes in Law or generally applicable regulatory programs affecting similarly situated concessionaires in [jurisdiction] generally; provided, further, that any such excluded item shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred to the extent it has a disproportionate adverse effect on the Project or the Concessionaire relative to other similarly situated Persons. For the avoidance of doubt, none of the following shall be excluded from 'Material Adverse Effect' by reason of the foregoing proviso: (i) any matter set forth on Schedule 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries), (ii) any project-specific enforcement action, order, fine, penalty, permit denial, suspension, or revocation, or (iii) any material expansion in scope, adverse finding, or binding determination arising out of the inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7."

  Conforming representation clean-up:

  "Section [3.7] (Regulatory Matters). Except as set forth on Schedule 3.7, there are no pending or, to [Party]'s Knowledge, threatened regulatory inquiries, investigations, or enforcement actions relating to the Project. The disclosure on Schedule 3.7 qualifies the representation in this Section [3.7] only and does not limit the definition of Material Adverse Effect or any closing condition, termination right, or indemnity referencing Material Adverse Effect or regulatory Loss."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 4 — Limitation Period / Survival Shortened for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Base draft / playbook / Exhibit B: Survival matrix on Exhibit B sets defined survival periods for fundamental, core operational/regulatory, and general representations (with fraud surviving indefinitely / to the applicable statute of limitations). Core representations — including those tied to authority, enforceability, key permits, and regulatory status — survive for the Exhibit B core period.

TxDOT markup: Imposes a new, shorter limitation / survival period on core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Schedule / exhibit interaction:
  • Exhibit B controls the survival architecture; the markup's shorter period is a direct conflict and, under the schedules-and-exhibits rule stated in the matter file, scheduled/exhibit terms control over general markup statements unless expressly amended by both parties with an updated Exhibit B.
  • Schedule 3.7 regulatory matters and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities often surface post-closing on timelines longer than an aggressively shortened core survival window; cutting survival strands indemnity for the precise risks already flagged.

Lender / surety:
  • Lender side letters frequently require that fundamental and core project representations survive at least through [construction completion / specified tail] consistent with Exhibit B; a shorter contractual survival can breach financing conditions or force a re-papering.
  • Surety claim and indemnity windows are calibrated to the contractual survival matrix; shortening core survival is a common surety re-underwrite trigger.

Controlling client instruction: ANY survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.

Risk rating: HIGH — WALK-AWAY

Recommendation: REJECT in full. No compromise on shortening core (or fundamental) survival below Exhibit B. Require express reaffirmation that Exhibit B remains controlling, and delete the markup's new limitation period as applied to core representations. General (non-core) representation survival may be discussed only within Exhibit B bands; core and fundamental are non-negotiable per client instruction.

Counter-proposal language:

  "Section [Y.Y] (Survival). The representations and warranties of the Parties contained in this Agreement shall survive the Closing for the periods set forth on Exhibit B (Survival Matrix), and no amendment, markup, or limitation period stated elsewhere in this Agreement shall shorten any survival period set forth on Exhibit B unless Exhibit B is expressly amended by a written instrument signed by both Parties that identifies the specific row(s) of Exhibit B being modified. Claims for Fraud or Willful Misconduct shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Any claim notice delivered in good faith before the applicable survival expiration shall preserve the claim until finally resolved. For the avoidance of doubt, the core representations identified on Exhibit B (including authority, enforceability, key permits, and regulatory status) shall survive for the full core period stated on Exhibit B, and any shorter limitation period appearing in any counterparty markup is rejected and of no force or effect."

  Exhibit B reaffirmation block (to be initialed):

  "The Parties reaffirm Exhibit B in the form attached to the firm draft dated [date], without modification to the survival periods for Fundamental Representations or Core Representations."

================================================================================
IV. CROSS-REFERENCE MATRIX — LENDER LETTERS, SURETY LETTERS, FINANCIAL MODEL
================================================================================

Item                         | Base Position        | TxDOT Markup           | Lender Letter Impact              | Surety Letter Impact             | Model Impact                         | Rating / Disposition
---------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------
Indemnity Cap                | Playbook full cap    | Silent reduction        | Conditionality / recovery gap     | Re-price or penal-sum pressure   | Lower recovery; contingency stress   | HIGH — Restore / special stack
Basket                       | Deductible           | Tipping                 | Neutral / slight positive         | Neutral                          | Modest recovery improvement          | CONCEDE — Clean tipping draft
MAE — Regulatory carve-out   | Project-specific in  | Carve-out covers Sch 3.7| MAE daylight vs. financing MAC    | Open regulatory requalify risk   | Contingency may not absorb Sch 3.7   | HIGH — Reject as to Sch 3.7
Survival — Core reps         | Exhibit B matrix     | Shortened limitation    | Financing covenant breach risk    | Claim-window misalignment        | Stranded post-closing recovery       | HIGH — WALK-AWAY; restore Ex. B

================================================================================
V. INTEGRATED NEGOTIATING POSTURE (PLAYBOOK-ALIGNED)
================================================================================

1. Lead with walk-away restoration of Exhibit B survival for core and fundamental representations. Do not trade survival for other concessions. Per controlling partner instruction, survival-period reduction ends the negotiation path on current terms.

2. Simultaneously reject the Schedule 3.7-covering MAE regulatory carve-out. Offer only the market carve-out for generally applicable law/regulatory programs with disproportionate-impact add-back, and an express save-out for Schedule 3.7 and project-specific enforcement.

4. Require a conforming set: definitions, damages limitation, Schedule 3.7 qualification language, Schedule 5.2 special indemnity, Exhibit B reaffirmation, and lender/surety bring-down or consent packs before signing.

5. Do not rely on, and do not incorporate, any position drawn from misfiled unrelated correspondence in the matter folder.

================================================================================

Dev. 1 — Indemnification cap silently reduced
  Rating:        HIGH
  Disposition:   REJECT silent reduction; restore base cap or expressly quantify with Schedule 5.2 special indemnity outside / above the general cap.

  Rating:        CONCEDE

  Rating:        HIGH
  Disposition:   REJECT as applied to Schedule 3.7 and project-specific regulatory action; limited general-change-in-law carve-out with disproportionate-impact add-back only.

================================================================================

1. Transmit this memorandum and the counter-proposal language packages (Sections III.1–III.4) to TxDOT counsel as a consolidated issues list marked "Exhibit B Survival — Walk-Away; Basket — Conceded."
2. Circulate lender and surety bring-down request packages highlighting cap, MAE, and survival positions; obtain written confirmation that restored Exhibit B survival and MAE-live treatment of Schedule 3.7 satisfy side-letter conditions.
3. Update the financial model sensitivity case for (a) restored cap vs. silent reduced cap and (b) Schedule 3.7 adverse-outcome tail; confirm DSCR / reserve sizing under the recommended positions.

5. Escalate immediately if TxDOT re-asserts any survival shortening; per client instruction, that issue terminates current-path negotiations.

================================================================================
VIII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

Of the four TxDOT deviations, one (basket conversion to tipping) is accepted under the controlling deal-team instruction and should be documented cleanly. The silent indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs that neutralize Schedule 3.7 are high-risk shifts against playbook, lender/surety, and model assumptions and should be rejected or tightly cabined as set forth above. The shortened survival period for core representations contradicts Exhibit B and is a client walk-away item — it must be restored in full as a condition to further engagement on residual issues.

This memorandum addresses every identified deviation in the Counterparty markup, reconciled against the base draft, negotiation playbook, lender and surety letters, financial model, Schedules 3.7 and 5.2, Exhibit B, and the controlling (latest) deal-team correspondence. Misfiled unrelated correspondence was disregarded.
